gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Logitech's own US G435 page lists the LIGHTSPEED dongle for PC, Mac, PS4 and PS5 only, while an image caption on the same page says 'Compatible with Xbox, PS5, PC, Nintendo Switch / Switch 2'. None of them states that EKSA sells a replacement Mako BT 2.4 GHz dongle for $9.99, or that EKSA's tri-mode headsets come with per-mode exclusions such as Bluetooth not working on PS4/PS5 and Xbox working only by 3.5 mm cable.
standout_why: SoundGuys (cited) says only that the G435 'supports both USB dongle and Bluetooth connections, so you can use it across PC, PlayStation, and mobile'. It names no dongle connector, has no Xbox or Switch statement and has no per-mode limits. Its only dongle-connector detail is for the Arctis 1 ('USB-C dongle… includes a USB-A adapter'). I could not read the bodies of RTINGS wireless, RTINGS under-$50, PC Gamer or Vaagame: WebFetch returned only navigation, the page title or a certificate error, and Bash curl was not approved. So I can't rule out that those pages carry Xbox or Switch notes. ChatGPT's own third answer already warns that 'many inexpensive wireless gaming headsets won't connect to [Xbox] wirelessly', so the general Xbox warning is not new. The new parts are the maker-sourced split by connection mode and the replacement-dongle accessory.
decides: This confirms the platform-first structure rather than changing the pick. For a PS5 or PC buyer, any of the 2.4 GHz picks works through the dongle. For an Xbox buyer, no candidate under $50 is maker-documented to work wirelessly, so the page should route them to a 3.5 mm-capable model (EKSA E900 BT or Mako BT) used wired, not to the G435, which has no cable mode on our current page. The G435's 'Xbox' caption should not be repeated without the maker's per-mode document. The Mako BT's $9.99 replacement dongle is a plus for buyers who worry about losing the receiver.
